subject: Hospitality
title: Smart Room Technology
description: A quick, practical guide to Smart Room Technology.

hook.text: In a smart hotel room, your phone controls lights, curtains, temperature, and TV. Some rooms learn your preferences automatically.

buildup.text: Voice assistants like Alexa for Hospitality take room service orders, set alarms, and answer questions—hands-free convenience.

discovery.text: Sensors detect occupancy: lights dim when you leave, thermostats adjust, and housekeeping is alerted when the room is empty.

twist.text: Many guests find smart rooms frustrating. Unfamiliar controls, connectivity issues.

climax.text: The key lesson: technology should simplify, not complicate. If a guest can't figure out the lights, the 'smart' room has failed.

punchline.text: Smart when it simplifies, stupid when it doesn't. Tech must serve comfort.

quiz.question: What is the main risk of smart room technology?
options: Unfamiliar controls and connectivity issues can frustrate guests
